noteGrp.note: A Syriac historical romance. Framed as a report composed by Jovian’s official Apolloris for the abbot Abdel to aid in converting pagans, the text details the reigns of Emperors Julian and Jovian. The first portion traces Julian’s youth and accession following the death of Constantine the Great, highlighting his anti-Christian persecutions through the trial and confession of Bishop Eusebius of Rome. The second portion covers Julian’s fatal campaign against Persia, followed by Emperor Jovian’s efforts to negotiate a peace treaty and restore the Church.

note.quote: ܐܦ ܐܠܗܐ ܛܝܒܘܬܐ ܕܕܘܒܪܘܗܝ: ܘܫܟܒ ܥܠ ܥܪܣܐ ܕܢܝܚܗ ܒܥܠܡܐ. ܘܐܬܟܢܫ ܠܘܬ ܥܡܗ. ܘܐܬܬܘܣܦ ܥܠ ܐܒܗܘܗܝ:
GOD gave him the reward of his conduct. He lay down on the bed which brought him rest from this world; he rejoined his people, and was gathered unto his fathers.
ܘܥܠ ܥܪܣܐ ܕܢܝܚܗ ܗܘܐ ܥܘܢܕܢܗ. ܒܫܢܬ ܫܬܡܐܐ ܘܫܒܥܝܢ ܘܚܡܫ ܒܡܢܝܢܐ ܕܝܘܢܝܐ ܘܡܝܬ ܙܕܝܩܐܝܬ. ܘܐܬܩܒܪ ܒܐܝܩܪܐ ܐܝܟ ܕܫܘܝܢ ܗܘܘ ܕܘܒܪܘܗܝ.
On the bed of repose, his death occurred in the year 675, according to the Greek reckoning. The just man died; and was buried with dignity, such as the conduct of his life deserved.
